prompt: The client asks: "Should we launch our ride-hailing app in a new city?" Fact sheet: the city has 2 million people; the incumbent holds 85% share; drivers earn 20% more with the incumbent; acquiring a customer would cost $40, against a $35 lifetime value; entry requires a $5M license; the city hosts a large music festival. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: Don't enter this city. Acquiring a customer would cost $40 against a $35 lifetime value, the incumbent holds 85% share and pays drivers 20% more, and entry needs a $5M license. The main risk is that the incumbent stumbles and leaves an opening, so the next step is to monitor the market and revisit if acquisition costs fall.
options.feedback: Right. It leads with the answer, backs it with the numbers that matter, and gives a risk and a next step.

options.text: On one hand, acquiring a customer would cost $40 against a $35 lifetime value, the incumbent holds 85% share and pays drivers 20% more, and entry needs a $5M license. On the other hand, there is the risk that the incumbent stumbles and leaves an opening. It depends on the client's priorities, so I'd want more analysis before committing either way.
options.feedback: This never takes a position. Commit to an answer, then name the risk.

options.text: Don't enter this city. The city hosts a large music festival each year. Acquiring a customer would cost $40 against a $35 lifetime value, the incumbent holds 85% share and pays drivers 20% more, and entry needs a $5M license.
